{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"For a few breaths, nobody moved.

Then the woman with the bell rang it once. The clear note passed over the meadow, and every carved bird turned its stone head toward the sound.

Tomas let out a shaky laugh. “Is that good?”

“It means the path is open,” she said. “Or that something has heard us.”

Mara looked down at the blank page. A bead of blue ink trembled at the tip of her pen, though she hadn’t touched it. Slowly, letters appeared beneath the empty space.

Not names this time, but a question:

WHO WILL KEEP THE STORY?

The brothers had stopped at the edge of the grass. The older one—if he was older—looked back at the well. “We can’t remember everything,” he said.

“No,” Mara replied. “But we can remember you.”

She wrote their names again, then added the place where they had been found: under the hill, beside the well. The ink sank into the paper and spread like a tiny dark pool.

The woman’s bell gave a faint answering chime.

From somewhere beyond the meadow came the sound of a door opening. A narrow track appeared between the trees, silvered with moonlight, though the sky above them was still pale with morning.

Tomas glanced at Mara. “Are we going?”

She shut the book. Its cover was warm beneath her palm.

“Not yet,” she said. “First we take them home.”

The brothers stood together, their hands clasped. Behind them, the well held no reflection at all. But as the four travelers set off across the grass, the blank page began to fill with a map."}
